title: The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers
main_claim: For two independent half-plane Temperleyan matchings, the loops of their superposition, mapped into the disk by F(z)=(z-i)/(z+i), converge in law to nested CLE_4 as δ→0. The convergence is in the curve topology (every macroscopic loop matched as an unparametrized curve), along the full mesh limit, and the family is tight in the interior-collection space.

issues.location: Sec 1.4, Theorem 1.2 (cylindrical convergence), used in Lemma 5.1
issues.description: The identification of the limit depends entirely on Basok–Izyurov arXiv:2501.01574v1, Thm 4.2(2) / Eq. (4.17). This is an unrefereed preprint, used as a black box: half-plane Temperleyan law, all nested generations, reduced laminations for fixed punctures. This is an external dependency, not a gap in the paper's own argument.
issues.evidence: Intro: 'The precise input is equation (4.17) of the cited theorem in the January 2, 2025 preprint version.' Every later identification step goes through this theorem. I could not check the hypotheses against BI offline.

coverage:
I read all five sections in full: transfer, short-segment, localization, identification and the introduction with its imported inputs.

Checked:
- The exact rectangle partition function (eq. rectangle-partition) against a brute-force dimer count for m in {1,3,5,7,9} and n in {3,5,7}. It matches exactly.
- The spectrum: λ_l=2cos(πl/(2p+2)) from BB^T, and u_l=arsinh(cos(πl/(n+1))).
- The sector-penalty exponent, the all-state sum 2∏(1+e^{-tu})^2, and the cap normalization algebra.
- The tear/marked-cap norm bound and the lower bound 2^{-2k}. The closing of the k→k^2 recursion, including the monotonicity of k_j/(4^j log k_j).
- The insertion parity sign. A global sign convention is irrelevant because only |contraction| is bounded.
- The color-contraction values uv/2 and -t_g t_g'/4, including sink admissibility and the arc orientation sign cancellation.
- The positivity of the product a(a-e).
- The nesting-depth parity formula, equal depths of the outermost chain members, the two-chain alternating-sum positivity with constants q^2/8 and q^2/16, and the cap-weight halving lemma.
- Wilson-net localization, recovery of primal directions, and the corollaries.
- Aizenman–Burchard-style reparametrization: q_j ≤ N_{r_j/2}+1, and the modulus of continuity.
- Generic test lines; the signature coupling via the regular conditional kernel; singleton exclusion.
- The slow-grid diagonal argument. The index equalities and the geometric tests use the same stage-k grid, so the opposite-sign violation lands on a level-r_n interval as required.
- Trace/degree identification, the Jordan-line lemma, no-backtracking via lifts, and restriction to the interior space.

Not checked: the content of the BI, BC and BW theorems themselves.
